questions.q: In what order is the first kit put together?
options: Aircraft → batteries and charger → goggles for the aircraft → radio for its receiver
Radio → simulator → video system and goggles → aircraft → batteries and charger
Charger and batteries → aircraft → radio → goggles
questions.explain: You buy from the long-lived to the consumable: the radio lasts the longest and is needed for the simulator, the goggles lock the ecosystem and are chosen before the aircraft.

questions.q: A radio is sold in “ELRS” and “4-in-1” variants. How do they differ for a beginner in 2026?
options: The 4-in-1 includes ELRS and three more protocols
The ELRS version does not work with a simulator
The 4-in-1 cannot do ELRS: it is for FrSky, FlySky, DSM
There is no difference, the protocol is selected in EdgeTX
questions.explain: A multiprotocol module is four radio chips running the MULTI-Module firmware; ExpressLRS is not among its protocols. Modern BNFs come with ELRS receivers.

questions.q: You have DJI Goggles N3. Which air unit will not work with them?
questions.explain: According to the DJI specification the N3 work with the O4 and O4 Pro; according to Oscar Liang's review the N3 have no O3 support. Goggles from other brands do not work with DJI air units at all.

questions.q: Three aircraft on analog, and you decided to move to DJI. What does the price of the move consist of?
options: New goggles and an air unit for every aircraft
New goggles, a DJI radio and new antennas for the aircraft
questions.explain: DJI goggles do not show analog, and the video transmitter of every aircraft has to be of the same system: $229–499 for the goggles plus $130–229 per aircraft.

questions.q: The radio has been updated to ExpressLRS 4.1.0. A new whoop with an SPI receiver on Betaflight 2025.12 does not link. Why?
options: For 4.x the binding phrase must be set again on both devices
The SPI receiver there is ELRS 3, and it is incompatible with 4.x
The whoop uses a different frequency band
questions.explain: The SPI receiver's protocol is executed by Betaflight; in 2025.12 that is over-the-air version 3. Major versions 3.x and 4.x do not link by any means, and ELRS Configurator does not flash such a receiver.

questions.q: The dry weight of a 3.5" is 158 g. A 4S 850 mAh battery weighs 98 g, a 4S 650 mAh — 76 g. With which battery does the aircraft stay under 250 g?
questions.explain: 158 + 98 = 256 g — above the threshold; 158 + 76 = 234 g. You weigh it with the battery and everything attached.

questions.q: Four 6S 1200 mAh batteries are charged in parallel at 1C. What charger power is needed?
questions.explain: I = 4 × 1.2 = 4.8 A; U = 6 × 4.2 = 25.2 V; P = 25.2 × 4.8 ≈ 121 W. A charger with a 60 W supply will reduce the current and take twice as long.

questions.q: Which first aircraft leaves the fewest regrets?
options: An RTF kit, to add aircraft to its radio later
A BNF whoop or 3.5" for your own radio and goggles
A 7" long range with GPS to grow into
questions.explain: A BNF flies right away and works with the radio and goggles that will stay. A 5" is dangerous and expensive to crash, the radio and goggles of RTF kits are usually no good for the next aircraft, and a self-build is for the second aircraft.
